title: Payment Standing and the Lease Term Agreement Renewal Increase Cap
content:
The standing cap reduction applied in pricing a like-program renewal offer line on a Lease Term Agreement is set by the lease's payment record on the Apartment Home Lease: a lease with no returned payment dated fewer than 12 full calendar months before the handling date and with ACH autopay enrolled reduces the cap by 0.5 percentage points; a lease with no such returned payment and without autopay enrolled reduces it by 0.25 percentage points; a lease with such a returned payment receives no standing reduction. The cap reduced is the company cap, the expiring term program's renewal increase cap. The reduction never takes the company cap below zero.

## What the desk reads

- **Returned payments.** The payment returns on the Apartment Home Lease — payments dishonoured and returned by the bank or card network — dated fewer than 12 full calendar months before the handling date.
- **Autopay.** Whether recurring ACH autopay is enrolled on the lease.

## Decision table

| Returned payment in the 12-month span | ACH autopay enrolled | Standing cap reduction |
|---|---|---|
| None | Yes | 0.5 percentage points (0.005) |
| None | No | 0.25 percentage points (0.0025) |
| One or more | Yes | none |
| One or more | No | none |

## Boundary of the 12-month span (hypothetical dates)

With a handling date of 10 September, a return dated 11 September of the previous year is fewer than 12 full calendar months before the handling date and counts; a return dated 10 September of the previous year is a full 12 months before it and does not count.

## Worked case (hypothetical)

A Flexible Lease (6-9 Months) term with a company cap of 9 percent, on a lease enrolled in ACH autopay and with no return in the span: the cap is reduced by 0.5 percentage points, to 8.5 percent. The same lease without autopay: 8.75 percent. With a return in the span: 9 percent.
